Next month's 26th marks the first anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit its report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports indicate that the government has activated the head of department accountability system to investigate the administrative responsibility for the fire and has redeployed administrative officers to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (the 6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism has been activated, stating that the government has made a series of deployments and will implement reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The Stanley luxury residence One Stanley was revealed to have steel reinforcement not matching the plans. Lee stated that the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With multiple engineering projects being exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches great importance to the quality of construction in Hong Kong, which concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

Nearly a year after the Wang Fuk Court fire, the independent committee is expected to submit its report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports stated that two administrative officers, former Deputy Secretary of Security Bureau Mo Kwan-yu and Sports Liaison Officer Choi Kin-pan, which would celebrate its 60th anniversary on the 1st of next month, will provide support work in the investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically responsible for preliminary work on administrative accountability.

Chief Executive John Lee met the media before attending the Executive Council today and was asked whether the incident is true? With the head of department accountability system activated to investigate responsibility, does it mean that even with a report, if official accountability is involved, there will not be immediate results, and how long must the public wait?

Lee stated that he had made it clear from the beginning that after the independent committee submits its report, he would actively study and follow up on recommendations, carry out reforms and announce details. He did not directly respond to whether administrative officers have been redeployed to prepare preliminary investigation work, only saying that "the government has made a series of deployments during this period," emphasizing that after the report is submitted, based on its content, "comprehensive reforms will be implemented as soon as possible in the short term, and accountability will be pursued," with detailed announcements to be made at that time.

Lee stated that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms will be implemented and accountability pursued as soon as possible based on the report's content. (File photo)

Lee also reiterated multiple times that improvement measures are urgent and cannot be delayed. Therefore, when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced seven priority improvement measures, including banning smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire safety installations, enhancing disciplinary and punitive measures for professionals and contractors, improving compliance operations of owners' corporations, studying the criminalization of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, establishing pre-qualification lists for consultants and contractors, and studying solutions to better assist the public on professional aspects of works.

The Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that provides advice to the Chief Executive on civil service recruitment, promotion, and disciplinary matters. The head of department accountability system was proposed by Chief Executive John Lee in last year's Policy Address. Based on the severity of departmental issues, a two-tier investigation mechanism has been established. If the issue is less serious in nature or is an isolated incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the head of department. If the department has serious problems, or involves extensive, repetitive systemic issues, or may involve the role of the head of department, the investigation小组 led by the "Public Service Commission" will conduct a second-tier investigation.

The luxury residence One Stanley was revealed to have units with steel reinforcement not matching the plans. Lee stated he would not comment on cases still under investigation, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley "steel pulling" – requests Development Bureau to monitor investigation

Recently, construction projects have been exposed for problems one after another, including the lift shaft tilting in the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples at a Tung Chung public housing estate not meeting strength standards, and floor slab steel reinforcement at the Stanley luxury residence One Stanley not matching the plans. When Lee was asked whether there are problems in construction and project supervision?

He responded to the One Stanley project issue, stating that the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "to ascertain whether construction quality and supervision were adequate, and will handle it strictly in accordance with the law." As the investigation is ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the case investigation. However, he emphasized that he attaches great importance to the quality of construction projects in Hong Kong, "paying attention to whether professionals related to the project have diligently supervised, and whether contractors have violated regulations during construction." He also pointed out that it concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will inevitably strictly enforce the law.

He has also requested the Development Bureau to enhance legal regulatory requirements and penalties for overall construction projects, ensuring the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punishing relevant personnel who violate regulations, and safeguarding the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen supervision and enhance the penalty system and sanctions, and the authorities will推进 the relevant work at full speed.

Recent attention has been drawn to the difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs. The government has stated that nursing demand exists in the long term, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has over 3,000 nursing vacancies, which graduates can apply for. (File photo)

Executive Councillor Cheung Yu-man criticizes "unions impersonating people" – Lee states demand exists in the long term

Discussion about the difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs has heated up recently. The source was a radio hosting call-in program after the Policy Address, where a Mr. Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in the disciplined services, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and his daughter who graduated from a nursing program was unemployed immediately after graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority's introduction of mainland medical personnel. Executive Council member Cheung Yu-man subsequently questioned whether it was the union "impersonating people on the phone at any time," stating that he firmly supports importing foreign talent.

When the reporter asked about the difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs, how to address the concentration of vacancies in experienced nurses? And how to respond to Executive Council members' remarks being accused of intensifying social conflicts? Lee stated that in every industry, there are situations where graduates do not seek employment immediately after graduation due to individual reasons, or where recruiting organizations select the most suitable candidates, "resulting in individual cases of not being hired." He emphasized that societal demand for nurses has always existed, especially given Hong Kong's continuous medical development and aging population trend, "so recruitment numbers will inevitably reflect this existing demand." He also alluded without naming names, saying "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, which allows everyone to clarify the issue more thoroughly."

Lee also pointed out that according to 2025/26 figures, there are approximately 4,000 potential nursing graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 applied for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has over 3,000 nursing vacancies, "nursing graduates can apply, and have the opportunity to be hired."

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier accepted interviews with multiple media outlets to clarify that the government's recruitment policy definitely prioritizes local talent. Lee also reiterated that based on the current number of nurses in the Hospital Authority, "99.8% are Hong Kong locally trained nurses," clearly implementing the local talent priority employment policy. He also pointed out that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, with the remaining 60% in other healthcare positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, private medical institutions, etc. He emphasized that societal demand for nurses exists in the long term. The government will, based on medical service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia to do a good job in planning medical training and manpower development.
